column3: The Hebrew states praise befits the upright without the added Him as its object in BSB.
The Hebrew explicitly names the ten-stringed instrument; BSB mentions ten strings without naming it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes all His work as in faithfulness; BSB says trustworthy.
The Hebrew leaves the lover unnamed and explicitly attaches the LORD’s name to loving devotion; BSB reverses these references.
The Hebrew calls them the heavens’ host; BSB specifies stars.
The Hebrew explicitly compares the gathered waters to a heap or wall; BSB describes piling them up.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes frustrating and thwarting as completed actions; BSB uses present verbs.
The Hebrew repeats generation and generation; BSB says all generations.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has completed verbs of looking and seeing; BSB has present verbs.
The Hebrew describes His gazing with a completed verb; BSB uses a present verb.
The Hebrew has their heart in the singular and says together; BSB has hearts of each.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the horse a lie for salvation; BSB calls it a vain hope.
The Hebrew has eye in the singular; BSB has eyes.
The Hebrew explicitly names their soul; BSB says them.
The Hebrew describes waiting with a completed verb; BSB says waits.
The Hebrew has our heart in the singular; BSB has hearts.
Close to the Hebrew.
